question: Does spelling normalisation improve sentiment classification?

config.ablation_note: hkey_vdrop = H-Key with V-drop; agreed after the settings were frozen, reported as an ablation, never used to choose settings. p-values are not corrected for multiple comparisons

features.rocchio: ltc tf-idf, cosine-normalised; nearest centroid by Euclidean distance
features.knn: ltc tf-idf, cosine similarity; majority vote, ties -> class of nearest neighbour

config.tuning: k chosen on dev by macro F1 (ties -> smaller k); test predicted once
config.significance: paired bootstrap, 1000 resamples of the test set, seed 42; delta = macro F1(mode) - macro F1(raw), same classifier; p = one-sided fraction of resamples with delta <= 0
config.hkey_settings_source: frozen; chosen on the E1 dev groups by strict pairwise F1 (results/e1_variants.json), before this run
config.comparison_metric: weighted F1 (support-weighted mean of per-class F1), as in Patwa et al. 2020 Sec. 3.1

published_reference.paper: Patwa et al. 2020, Table 3; Gopalan and Hopkins 2020
